title: MammaPrint™ Genetic Signature in the Brazilian Population, Analysis of Results and Clinical Outcomes (AGEMA-BRA) – Real World Study
content: Purpose: The MammaPrint™ (MP) 70-gene signature, identifies hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer patients with low genomic risk who are candidates for de-escalation of the systemic therapies employed. Knowing that MP was validated in an exclusively European cohort and understanding the heterogeneity of breast tumors in different populations, we proposed a study to analyze MP performance in the Brazilian population. Methods: Retrospective, prognostic evaluation, real-world cohort study of HR+, HER2- breast cancer patients who underwent MP in Brazil from January 2016 to December 2020 (AGEMA-BRA). Results: Of the 953 patients with high clinical risk, 407 (42.7%) had high genomic risk, and 546 (57.3%) had low genomic risk to MP. In the analysis of epidemiological, clinical, and anato-mopathological data correlating high and low risk to MP, and among the subgroups with low-risk, ultra-low risk, high-risk 1 and high-risk 2, only the histological grade showed statistical significance. Distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) was 97.8% and overall survival (OS) was 99.8% with a mean follow-up of 40.8 months, with no difference between high and low genomic risk. Conclusions: Applying the MP signature in the AGEMA-BRA cohort enabled greater chemotherapy de-escalation with better DMFS than observed in the MINDACT pivotal study. Equivalent DMFS and OS results between high and low genomic risk carriers demonstrate the appropriate selection of patients by MP to receive or not receive adjuvant chemotherapy. These data make it possible to validate the performance of the signature in the Brazilian population and confirm the importance of testing it in different populations.
